apply.title: Stevens - First-Year Applicants (requirements, test policy, English)

test_policy.notes: Test-optional for first-year applicants through the fall 2029 entry term, with exceptions: the Accelerated Pre-Medicine and Pre-Law programs still require scores (Pre-Med: SAT 1400 or ACT 32 in one sitting, taken before the Nov 1 deadline). Scores may be self-reported in the applicant portal. Stevens has no minimum GPA or test score.

requirements.notes: Two letters of recommendation (teacher or school counselor preferred), official transcript and essay. Interview optional for most applicants (international applicants are strongly recommended to interview; InitialView accepted). Music and Visual Arts & Technology applicants are strongly encouraged to submit a portfolio. CSS Profile (code 2819) is required to be considered for Stevens need-based aid; FAFSA for federal/state aid. The timeline page gives month/day only (no year); dates below are applied to the fall 2027 cycle.

deadlines.label: Early Decision I
deadlines.notes: Binding. Notified by Dec 15. Deposit due Jan 10. CSS Profile and FAFSA due Nov 15.

deadlines.label: Early Action
deadlines.notes: Non-binding. Notified by Feb 1; deposit May 1 (Mar 5 for priority housing/registration). CSS Profile and FAFSA due Dec 15.

deadlines.label: Early Decision II
deadlines.notes: Binding. Notified by Feb 15. Deposit due Mar 1. CSS Profile and FAFSA due Jan 5.

deadlines.label: Regular Decision
deadlines.notes: Non-binding. Notified by Apr 1; deposit May 1. CSS Profile and FAFSA due Jan 5.

english_policy.waiver_notes: Waivers considered case by case for international students who have studied in the US for at least 3 years. Alternative: SAT Evidence-Based Reading & Writing 550+. Native English speakers exempt.

english.notes: Listed on the first-year page; not listed on the international students page.

aid.notes: International students are not eligible for federal aid; Stevens awards a limited number of merit scholarships to international students. The CSS Profile (code 2819) is required to be considered for institutional scholarships. Whether international applicants receive need-based grants is not stated on the page.
